newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA worried about Australia corporate loans - paper.
newsitem.headline: RBA worried about Australia corporate loans - paper.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has told international banks operating in Australia it is worried about a deterioration in the the quality of corporate loans, The Australian Financial Review reported on Tuesday.

"(RBA Governor Ian Macfarlane's) concerns, which recalled the financial climate of the 1980s, were raised at the central bank's regular six-monthly meeting with international banks operating in Australia," the Financial Review said.
"Bankers who were at the meeting said Macfarlane was worried that the local and overseas banks were offering cheap loans with lenient terms," the newspaper said.
"The Reserve Bank obviously is a bit concerned about a deterioration in loan documentation, in margins," Deutsche Bank Australia chief executive Klaus Albrecht told the Financial Review.
Another banker told the Financial Review the Reserve Bank's concerns reflected the agenda currently being pushed by wholesale bankers.
"The Reserve Bank is picking up on the banks' concerns, and a consensus view between the Reserve Bank and the banks is emerging," the bank said.
"It's probably the threat of the capital markets as much as anything. If you don't have a flow of loan assets you have a declining book and if you have a declining book, you have declining income."
